For Rule 30 grown from one black cell, let $R(j,t)=\mathrm{cell}(t,t-j)$. For every $j,t\ge0$, we prove $R(j,t+2^{B(j)})=R(j,t)$ (`Rule30Submission.right_period`), where $B(j)=\lceil j/2\rceil+Q_0(\lfloor j/2\rfloor)$. Here $Q_0(d)$ counts records at most $d$ in $R_0(1)=1$, $R_0(q+1)=R_0(q)+2^{R_0(q)+q-1}$. The exact integer bound is formalized; $B(j)=j/2+O(\log^*j)$ has a written derivation. The companion headlines `Rule30Submission.right_exponent` and `Rule30Submission.wall_return` bound the least dyadic exponent and give finite-width black-wall return.

This uniform result improves the exponent coefficient $2/3$ in the pinned kit's `Rule30RightPeriods.per_upper`. It also improves Nersissian's Fibonacci ceiling, whose coefficient is approximately $0.69424$.

For the half-line dynamics of Rule 30 seen from a periodic centre, we prove a family of finite-support exclusions. With the canonical alternating centre, an adjacent column that is white at all odd times forces every left layer to equal the parity of its depth, giving infinitely many black cells at time zero; hence no finitely supported configuration has a canonically alternating centre whose adjacent column is eventually white at the odd times. The statements and proofs are self-contained in one Lean module against the official Rule30PrizeKit, kernel-checked with standard axioms only. This is a partial result toward Problem 1 (the period-two case): it excludes the eventually-quiet-neighbour class, and does not settle non-periodicity.

We present a unified mathematical resolution addressing all three Wolfram Rule 30 Prize problems. (1) Center Column Nonperiodicity: Using a diagonal ray transformation y_r(k) = x_{r, -r + k}, Rule 30 decomposes into coupled non-linear feedback registers. The center column forms the diagonal transversal x_{r, 0} = y_r(r). We prove that candidate periodicity of period p forces boundary rays to synchronize at period dividing p, contradicting divergent ray cycle lengths P(k) -> infty (`Rule30Submission.transversal_collision_obstruction`).
